entries.title: Abelian sheaves on finite sites
entries.purpose: Compare sheafification and cohomology routes on finite Alexandrov sites.
entries.algorithm: Build rational restriction matrices, matching-family kernels, plus construction, pointwise limits and Cech/derived-limit complexes.
entries.domain: Pseudocircle and pseudo-2-sphere; constant Q, a nonseparated presheaf and a monodromy -1 local system.
entries.arithmetic: Exact rational linear algebra and kernel/rank computations over Q.
entries.validation: Functor laws, separated/sheaf conditions, point-route dimensions and kernel/cokernel dimensions are checked; the sphere cover deliberately misses H² when it is not Leray.
entries.limitations: Rational coefficients omit torsion. Dimensionwise checks of exactness/comparison must not be described as a machine proof of the general sheafification theorem.
entries.prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

(check "i is not right exact: the unit Q -> a(Q) is a map of presheaves with cokernel of dimension 1 exactly at the disconnected open {a, b} and 0 elsewhere"
(check "pseudocircle: the cover by U_c and U_d is Leray and the three routes agree, (1, 1, 0) for Q and (0, 0, 0) for the monodromy -1 local system over Q"

(check "pseudo-2-sphere: the derived limit gives (1, 0, 1, 0), while the only cover by maximal opens has the pseudocircle as its intersection (not acyclic), so both Cech routes give (1, 0, 0, 0) and miss H^2: the Leray condition fails, as in the finite-spaces and descent examples"

entries.literature_review: On a finite T₀ space (Alexandrov topology), sheaves are the same as presheaves on the poset of points (McCord); sheafification a = (−)⁺⁺ is exact and left adjoint to the inclusion (Mac Lane–Moerdijk III.5); and sheaf cohomology equals the derived functors of the limit over the points, which Čech cohomology of a cover computes when the cover is Leray (Bredon III.4). The program computes all three statements over Q on the pseudocircle (the 4-point model of S¹) and the pseudo-2-sphere (the 6-point model of S²), including the case where the Leray hypothesis fails.

A. K. Bousfield, D. M. Kan, Homotopy Limits, Completions and Localizations, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 304, Springer (1972).
G. E. Bredon, Sheaf Theory, 2nd ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 170, Springer (1997).

entries.literature_review: On the Fermat sextic surface X₆² ⊂ P³ the Picard number is 86 (85 primitive Hodge characters plus the hyperplane class). Shioda (1979) shows the 108 lines span only the 62-dimensional part carried by the 61 'standard' characters; Aoki (1987) constructs further curves (for p = 2 and p = 3) to reach the remaining characters, and Villaflor Loyola's period formula (Manuscripta Math.) identifies the primitive class of a complete-intersection curve with the class of a Jacobian determinant in the Griffiths Jacobian ring. The program computes, by that formula, the character support of each family and reports how many of the 85 nontrivial Hodge characters the lines and Aoki's two curve families cover together.

The program computes the chain from the nerve of G (the bar construction, a model of BG) through integral homology and the twists to the state sums on S³, RP³ and T³, and checks each value against the closed formulas.
